quarterly_data.signal: CPO remains at the incubation stage - how the cooperation models and mass-production timing shake out is not yet clear - but management views optical as inevitable as bandwidth grows: beyond the two small announced customers there are large customers actively engaging, still too early to disclose. quarterly_data.quarter: GUC (Global Unichip) press release: GUC Announces 2nm 16 Gbps HBM4E IP (09-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: GUC announced that its HBM4E PHY and Controller IP is design-ready and has been adopted in customer AI ASICs (customers not named). Implemented on TSMC's N2P process, the HBM4E PHY has taped out on TSMC CoWoS-L advanced packaging. Building on GUC's silicon-proven 12 Gbps HBM4 IP on TSMC N3P, the HBM4E IP pushes data transfer speeds up to 16 Gbps across all signed-off operating conditions (GUC claims industry-leading power efficiency and a compact area), with its proprietary interposer layout optimized for SI/PI across TSMC CoWoS packaging configurations. A face-up variant is engineered as a bottom die in TSMC SoIC-X, with dedicated TSVs for signal pull-out and feedthrough power delivery to top dies; the IP incorporates proteanTecs interconnect monitoring. CTO Igor Elkanovich said uniting face-up HBM, face-up UCIe and GLink-3D IPs gives GUC a complete interface IP portfolio for 3D SoIC architectures.
quarterly_data.figure: HBM4E up to 16 Gbps on TSMC N2P (from 12 Gbps HBM4 on N3P); PHY taped out on CoWoS-L; adopted in customer AI ASICs

quarterly_data.signal: Teradyne announced Iris 100, which it calls a production-ready ("production-proven") optical test platform for microLED devices. It measures every individual emitter in an array with a spectrometer and high-resolution camera (spectral response, per-pixel luminance and uniformity), integrates directly with the Teradyne UltraFLEXplus platform for combined optical and electrical test, runs on Teradyne's IG-XL software to detect dead/stuck pixels and cluster defects early in manufacturing, and uses a NIST-traceable calibration workflow to correlate lots, wafers and manufacturing sites. It supports wafer and final test, with a roadmap to support photodetector test in the same insertion. Target devices are microLED arrays for AR microdisplays and optical data interconnects for AI data center architectures, which the company says contain hundreds of thousands to millions of individual emitters. Shannon Poulin, president of the Semiconductor Test division, said "MicroLED is shifting from lab to volume production for both AR microdisplays and, increasingly, optical interconnects, which are becoming foundational to how AI data centers scale beyond copper," and that Iris 100 delivers per-emitter test at production throughput "today on test infrastructure our customers already run at scale." Teradyne says it follows the Photon 100 introduction for silicon photonics and co-packaged optics test earlier this year. No customers named.

quarterly_data.signal: CHINA was 39% of Nova's business in 2024 and normalized to about 33% in 2025; management expects it to continue at AROUND 30% of sales. China has shorter lead times, which reduced visibility, but current trends give management confidence in steady Chinese investment and at least the nominal level of business in 2026. Because China focuses on mature nodes while advanced-node and DRAM investment grows, China's share of Nova's sales is expected to go down even if nominal sales stay flat.

quarterly_data.signal: 2025 revenue drivers: unit-driven revenue grew approximately 2% in 2025, in line with wafer starts, led by CMP consumables, liquid filtration and selective etch. CapEx-driven revenue declined 7%, matching the drop in industry fab construction CapEx, which the CEO described as 'down high single digits, call it seven ish percent'. The drop was most visible in the FOUP and Fluid Handling product lines in the APS division. About 75% of revenue is unit-driven and tracks MSI (wafer starts); the other 25% is tied to industry CapEx. Roughly two-thirds of that CapEx-related revenue follows fab construction spending and one-third follows WFE. Early in 2026, management said order patterns for these CapEx-linked product lines were already starting to recover.

About 40% of revenue comes from advanced logic, about 30% from mainstream logic and the rest from memory. Memory is about 30% of total revenue, split roughly half NAND and half DRAM.

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 logic and industry outlook: management expects Entegris to benefit from node transitions in both logic and memory. Rising demand for two-nanometer devices should meaningfully lift wafer output through 2026, and that node carries both higher content per wafer and strong share for Entegris. Advanced logic fab utilization is already near 100%, and customers are investing aggressively in more capacity. At the most advanced logic node, Entegris has secured strong POR (position of record) positions in CMP consumables, advanced deposition and implant materials, liquid purification and filtration, and wafer handling. The team is now focused on winning incremental share and PORs at subsequent advanced nodes. Separately, the CEO said it takes time to grow two-nanometer and to transition to new nodes such as 1.4 nanometer. Management expects 'middish single-digit' industry MSI (wafer starts) growth in 2026 and strong WFE growth. Fab construction CapEx should grow modestly after last year's high single-digit decline, weighted to the second half, with a bigger acceleration in 2027 as work starts on new fabs. Management flagged ongoing memory shortages as a possible second-half 2026 risk for mainstream end markets; guidance assumes no impact.
quarterly_data.figure: middish single-digit industry MSI growth expected in 2026; advanced logic utilization near 100%

quarterly_data.signal: NAND: the move from roughly 250 layers to approximately 300 layers is under way. Management expects more than 20% NAND bit growth in 2026, driven mainly by higher-layer, higher-capacity NAND rather than a big increase in wafer starts. Entegris expects a double-digit increase in its NAND content per wafer as customers move to higher layer counts and adopt new materials such as moly and selective etch. It has won strong POR positions in NAND deposition materials, CMP and selective etch. NAND utilization is around 85%, and layer-count increases are absorbing most of the remaining 15% of capacity, with fewer new wafer starts. If demand stays strong, flash makers will likely need to add significant fab capacity, setting up higher NAND MSI growth in 2027. The CEO said Entegris gains from both layer growth and wafer growth, with slightly more from a full wafer start.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 20% NAND bit growth expected in 2026; double-digit increase in NAND content per wafer; NAND utilization around 85%

quarterly_data.signal: DRAM, HBM and advanced packaging: DRAM capacity was nearly fully utilized at the end of 2025, and management expects it to stay that way through 2026. More DRAM is shifting from standalone DDR5 into HBM, which adds some content per wafer, though less than a new wafer start would. Management expects tight supply in HBM, DDR5 and advanced packaging to require additional fab capacity heading into 2027. Entegris is gaining traction in DRAM and HBM, particularly with CMP consumables and advanced packaging solutions. The CEO said advanced packaging revenue grew nicely in 2025, to 'roughly a $100 million plus minus', and should keep growing in 2026. Several product lines for advanced packaging are sampling now and more will sample later in the year, so the larger benefit is expected in 2027 and beyond.
quarterly_data.figure: advanced packaging revenue roughly $100 million (2025), expected to keep growing in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and capex: the multiyear manufacturing capex cycle that began in 2022 is complete.
